facts.raw_span: 1-month history of insidious-onset right lower abdominal pain
lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora
afebrile
blood pressure was 110/80 mmHg
firm, non-tender, mobile mass measuring approximately 12 cm × 10 cm in the right lower quadrant
bimanual pelvic examination confirmed a right adnexal mass
carcinoembryonic antigen 1.14 ng/mL
CA-125 21 U/mL
Transvaginal ultrasound showed multiple uterine fibroids and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion measuring 16.1 × 7.9 × 8.1 cm in the abdominopelvic region
a provisional diagnosis of a malignant ovarian tumor
double inferior vena cava was identified, with the left cava draining via the left renal vein to the right-sided cava

concepts.why: The patient's presentation with a right adnexal mass, a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa on ultrasound, and a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion on CT, along with a provisional diagnosis of a malignant ovarian tumor, supports this diagnosis.
The patient's imaging findings, including a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa and a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion on CT, could be consistent with an ovarian cystadenoma.
The patient's ultrasound showed multiple uterine fibroids, supporting a diagnosis of uterine leiomyoma.
The patient's lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora could be consistent with a lymphangioma.
The patient's CT scan incidentally identified a double inferior vena cava, which is an anatomical variation.

rationales.F01: Right lower abdominal pain is a common symptom of ovarian tumors.
rationales.F02: Lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora could be related to lymphatic malformation.
rationales.F05: A firm, non-tender, mobile mass in the right lower quadrant is highly suggestive of an ovarian tumor.
rationales.F06: Bimanual pelvic examination confirmed a right adnexal mass, which is consistent with an ovarian tumor.
rationales.F09: Transvaginal ultrasound showed multiple uterine fibroids and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa, which could be an ovarian tumor or a uterine leiomyoma.
rationales.F10: Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion, which is highly suggestive of an ovarian tumor.
rationales.F11: A provisional diagnosis of a malignant ovarian tumor was made based on imaging findings.
rationales.F12: A double inferior vena cava is a rare anatomical variation that is not directly related to the other conditions.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with a firm, non-tender, mobile mass in the right lower quadrant, a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa on ultrasound, and a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion on CT, along with the planned staging laparotomy with surgical excision, most strongly supports a malignant ovarian tumor, although the normal tumor markers and lack of definitive malignant features on imaging introduce some uncertainty.
